strengths: Novel application of test-time training (TTT) to streaming video understanding with well-motivated long-span prediction loss extending standard TTT formulations
Comprehensive system design combining TTTMEM layer, two-stage training, and modality-aware prompt-dependent memory reading that demonstrates strong empirical results
ELViM benchmark addresses an important unexplored evaluation scenario (episodic learning from long-past video experiences) with rigorous data pipeline preventing knowledge leakage

Extensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (Video-MME, LVBench, VideoEvalPro, StreamingBench) with thorough ablations clearly attributing performance gains; TTTMEM achieves comparable accuracy with 25% fewer tokens than merging
Consistent, substantial improvements especially on long-video understanding (14.2% on ELViM, 3-7% on standard benchmarks) and acceptable runtime overhead (0.1s per 3600 frames)
Clear presentation with effective architecture diagrams and detailed appendices; well-organized discussion of related work positioning contributions appropriately
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why a single gradient step per minibatch suffices for long-term consolidation across 3+ hour videos; connection between reconstruction and long-span prediction losses lacks formal rigor

Seemingly arbitrary hyperparameter choices: long-span prediction with T=2 predicts only ~24-32 frames despite 3-hour videos; appendix shows T=1-4 similar performance but no principled explanation for this range; chunk sizes and memory-reading parameters lack ablation

ELViM benchmark quality concerns: models achieve 98.7-99.3% accuracy on full videos (suggesting tasks may be easier than claimed), near-random 22.6% performance without video provides minimal signal, and modest scale (1849 questions, 1021 videos, 15 categories) with no inter-annotator agreement or human baselines

Incomplete architectural justification: audio tokens bypassing TTTMEM mentioned only in passing despite being significant simplification; deepstack embeddings excluded from TTTMEM in Appendix E due to computational cost, limiting mechanism expressiveness for Qwen3-VL's multi-stream design

Limited generalization analysis: all streaming evaluation at fixed 1 FPS without testing variable rates; no out-of-domain evaluation beyond tutorial/instructional videos; weak StreamingBench results (only 1.8% improvement) suggest possible overfit to long-video benchmarks

Reproducibility constraints: heavy dependence on Qwen3-VL backbone, ELViM generation via Gemini-2.5-Pro API, no reported random seeds or multiple runs; missing implementation details (θ initialization, exact gradient flow during TTTMEM)
